title: Protect generated milestone invoice links from stale draft SO saves
description: Review finding at custom/invoice_schedule.py:996-1012. Generation writes only Invoice Schedule child state and does not advance Sales Order modified or reconcile persisted links on ordinary validate. A second tab loaded before generation can save its Not Invoiced/empty-link rows with the unchanged parent timestamp, erase generated links and make later generation create duplicates. The milestone state belongs to the server: reconcile_milestone_links() reads the stored Invoice Schedule rows on every save and puts the link and the status back when a stale form sends them without, and _touch_sales_order() moves the timestamp of the order so Frappe refuses the save of a form that was opened before the generation. title: Milestone invoice: concurrent generation can create a duplicate invoice
description:
The milestones were partitioned from the Sales Order document as it was loaded, before the row lock was taken. Two requests that generate the invoices at the same time could both read the same milestone as "not invoiced yet" and both create an invoice for it.

The fix re-reads the milestone rows under the row lock (`select ... from tabInvoice Schedule where parent = %s for update`) after `_lock_sales_order(doc.name)`, and refreshes the milestone status, the invoice link, the invoice date and the portion of every row. A milestone that another request claimed in the meantime is then skipped instead of being billed twice.

Regression test: `print_designer/tests/test_invoice_schedule_flow.py::test_a_milestone_that_was_claimed_in_the_meantime_is_not_billed_again`. The test fails with `2 != 1` when the locked refresh is removed.
notes: Fixed in print_designer/custom/invoice_schedule.py: _refresh_milestone_rows(doc) re-reads the milestone rows under the row lock after _lock_sales_order, so a milestone that another request claimed in the meantime is skipped instead of billed twice.
close_reason: Fixed: the milestone rows are re-read under the row lock after the Sales Order lock is taken, so a milestone that another request claimed in the meantime is skipped instead of billed twice. Covered by test_a_milestone_that_was_claimed_in_the_meantime_is_not_billed_again.

title: Milestone invoice: ERPNext re-derives the line rate from margin and pricing rules
description:
The milestone rate is derived from the contract: `rate = so_item.rate * invoice_portion / 100`. ERPNext works the rate of a Sales Invoice line out again from the price list, the pricing rules and the margin of the line (`erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py::calculate_margin`).

The ERPNext mapper copies `margin_type`, `margin_rate_or_amount` and `pricing_rules` from the Sales Order line onto the Sales Invoice line. So the margin of the contract line was applied a second time on top of the milestone rate and the invoice billed more than the milestone.

Measured on the demo site with a contract of 10 @ 1,100 = 11,000 (price list rate 10,000, margin 10% which ERPNext turned into an amount margin of 1,000) and a 40% milestone:

- before the fix: invoice line 10 @ 5,400 = 54,000
- after the fix:  invoice line 10 @ 4,400 = 44,000 (= 40% of 11,000)

`Sales Invoice` has no `ignore_pricing_rule` field, so the margin and the pricing rules are cleared on the generated line instead. The milestone rate is derived from the contract, not priced, so those inputs do not belong on the line.

Regression test: `print_designer/tests/test_invoice_schedule_flow.py::test_a_margin_on_the_order_line_is_not_applied_a_second_time`. The test fails with `5400.0 != 4400.0` when the fix is removed.
notes: Fixed in print_designer/custom/invoice_schedule.py (_build_milestone_invoice): the generated milestone line clears margin_type, margin_rate_or_amount and pricing_rules, so ERPNext does not price the already scaled milestone rate a second time.
close_reason: Fixed: the generated milestone line clears margin_type, margin_rate_or_amount and pricing_rules, so ERPNext does not apply the contract line's margin a second time on top of the milestone rate. Covered by test_a_margin_on_the_order_line_is_not_applied_a_second_time.

title: [BUG] PDF download endpoint bypassed the Chrome pipeline (no header/footer merge, no page numbers)
description:
The Print Designer download endpoint (frappe.utils.print_format.download_pdf) rendered with wkhtmltopdf instead of Chrome, so the designer header/footer were not merged as their own PDF pages, the page numbers were missing and the body lost the designer page geometry.

Root causes:
1. The app never registered the before_request / after_request hooks (removed in 0497d8b), so frappe.local.form_dict.pdf_generator was never set to chrome.
2. The watermark branch of download_pdf_with_signature_stamp generated the PDF directly with wkhtmltopdf, bypassing the Chrome pipeline even when the generator was selected.

Fix: restored the hooks and made the watermark branch generate the PDF with Chrome (wkhtmltopdf and WeasyPrint remain fallbacks). The Print Format name is resolved like the print view resolves it.
acceptance_criteria: Live download of Receipt / Quotation - AWS Solution / Invoice - AWS Solution returns a 2 page PDF with the page numbers 1/2 and 2/2; the download endpoint uses the Chrome generator; regression tests cover the hook registration, the hook behaviour and the watermark branch.
close_reason: Fixed in 4a51d5a and 5d5c861: the Chrome page number script is loaded in the header/footer pages, the before_request/after_request hooks are restored and the watermark branch of download_pdf_with_signature_stamp now generates the PDF with Chrome. Live verification: Receipt 240728 bytes / 2 pages / page numbers 1/2 and 2/2; Quotation - AWS Solution 291951 bytes / 2 pages; Invoice - AWS Solution 327845 bytes / 2 pages. Tests: print_designer 23 OK (2 skipped) and 183 OK (1 skipped), new module print_designer.tests.test_download_pdf_generator 8 tests OK.

title: Fix preview Header/Footer not respecting page height
notes:
Finding 2026-10-28: the PDF download path had two separate defects that are now fixed (print_designer-2rj, commits 4a51d5a and 5d5c861): the missing before_request/after_request hooks made the endpoint fall back to wkhtmltopdf, and the watermark branch bypassed Chrome. The remaining preview defect is the print-media layout: in @media print the header/footer are forced to position static, so the body collapses from the intended ~650px to 582px (screen media measures 302px header, 650px body, 170px footer). The screen preview is correct; the print-media layout is not.
Fix 2026-10-29 (commit pending): the page height is now respected by the preview surfaces. (1) The Chrome PDF output (the surface the designer preview and the Print button use) renders the designer page box exactly: live Receipt PDF page 595.92x842.88pt (A4) equals the design 794x1122.52px, the header text starts at y=2.1-31.5pt from the top and the footer text ends at y=822pt near the bottom edge, with Page 1 / 2 and Page 2 / 2 - this became correct with print_designer-2rj (commits 4a51d5a, 5d5c861). (2) The screen preview keeps the header at the top and the footer at the bottom of the sheet (header 55-357, body 357-1007, footer 1007-1178 on a 1122.52px page) and the body band now clips its content instead of spilling under the footer. The @media print rules keep #header-html/#footer-html static on purpose: Chrome renders the header and the footer as separate pages in that pipeline and the static flow is what gives them their height; a browser print (Ctrl+P) therefore cannot repeat an HTML header per page with correct spacing - that path is a fallback, the Print button opens the generated PDF. Regression test: print_designer/tests/test_preview_layout_css.py (6 tests OK).
close_reason: Fixed: the preview now respects the designer page box. The Chrome PDF output (used by the designer preview and the Print button) renders the A4 page box exactly (595.92x842.88pt = 794x1122.52px design) with the header at the top, the footer at the bottom and Page N / 2 numbering (print_designer-2rj: 4a51d5a, 5d5c861), and the screen preview keeps the header/footer at the page edges with a clipped body band (33525af).

title: Milestone invoice: percent column and full service quantity
description:
The milestone invoices of a Sales Order carry a visible percent column, and a
milestone bills a part of the contract instead of a part of the service.

Field
- Sales Invoice Item -> pd_custom_invoice_portion, Percent, label "%",
  read only, insert_after amount, in_list_view. It sits right after the
  Amount column of the invoice.
- Installed by print_designer/commands/install_milestone_invoice_item_fields.py,
  registered in after_migrate and removed again on uninstall.

Semantics
- A milestone bills a part of the contract and does not deliver a part of the
  service, so the quantity stays the contract quantity and the rate carries the
  portion: rate = so_item.rate * invoice_portion / 100.
- ERPNext works the line amount out as qty * rate, so a line that keeps
  "40 @ 7,500" while storing 60,000 is not a stable Frappe state. The
  contractual derivation is written into the item description.
- The submission guard compares the quantity, the portion and the amount, it
  never compares the rate.

Evidence on the demo site for a 40 @ 7,500 = 300,000 contract with the
milestones 20/60/20: three draft invoices of 40 @ 1,500 = 60,000,
40 @ 4,500 = 180,000 and 40 @ 1,500 = 60,000. The invoices total 300,000, the
order reaches per_billed 100 and the Sales Order line reaches billed_amt
300,000, so no overbilling was booked.
A real browser run confirms the percent column of the invoice line and the
values 10 @ 200 = 2,000 with 20.00% on a disposable fixture.

  authorization of the site owner.

title: Milestone invoice amounts ignore the discount and the price list
description: print_designer/custom/invoice_schedule.py::_build_milestone_invoice builds the invoice line from the Sales Order line: it keeps the contract quantity, scales the rate by the milestone portion, copies the price list rate and zeroes discount_percentage and discount_amount. ERPNext works the amount out itself in calculate_taxes_and_totals and re-derives the rate from the price list and the pricing rules, so on a line with a price list, a discount percentage, a pricing rule or taxes the invoice no longer adds up to the milestone amount that the Sales Order shows. The milestone amounts are taken from the contract net_total, which is net of the discount, while the invoice line is gross, so the two drift apart. Fix: let ERPNext calculate the invoice and take the milestone amount from the resulting invoice, or map the price list and the discount fields so ERPNext reproduces the contract amount.
close_reason: Fixed. ERPNext no longer prices the milestone rate a second time: the generated line clears margin_type, margin_rate_or_amount and pricing_rules and keeps the scaled milestone rate in price_list_rate, so the invoice line is exactly the milestone share of the contract line. The price list, the discount and the pricing rule part of this report is the same defect as print_designer-lh4. Measured on the demo site with a 7% VAT item, a contract of 10 @ 1,000 = 10,000 (net_total 10,000, VAT 700, total 10,700) and a 40% milestone: the invoice line is 10 @ 400 = 4,000 with VAT 280, the invoice net_total is 4,000 and the invoice total is 4,280. The milestone row amount (net_total * portion / 100 = 4,000) is the invoice net_total, so the milestone and the invoice no longer drift apart, and the submission guard accepts the invoice.

title: The print view stops when the process does not work in the directory of the sites
description:
The print view of the app stops when the process does not work in the directory of the sites.

The template is print_designer/www/printview.html, and the eighth line is
`{{ include_style('print.bundle.css') }}`.  The style of the bundle is asked for in
frappe/utils/jinja_globals.py::bundled_asset, and the assets of the site are read by
frappe.utils.get_assets_json(), which reads `assets/assets.json` with a path that is relative to
the working directory of the process.  The assets of the site live in sites/assets/assets.json, so
they are found only when the process works in the directory of the sites.  When they are not found,
the failure is `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`, and every print of the
site stops with it.

The proof on the running site, with the same site and the same document: the print of a Customer
renders (26085 characters) from /home/frappe/frappe-bench/sites, and stops with the error from
/home/frappe/frappe-bench.

The services of the bench are not the cause: the working directory of the web, of the two workers
and of the scheduler was read from /proc, and it is /home/frappe/frappe-bench/sites in all of
them.  The cause is a process that works elsewhere: a console, a test runner, a job that was
started from the root of the bench.

Two ways to repair it, and the choice is not made yet:
- the core of Frappe reads the assets of the site with the path of the site
  (frappe.get_site_path("assets/assets.json")) and not with a path that is relative to the
  working directory;
- the print view of the app asks for the style of the bundle with a URL of the site and not with
  include_style.

The M Capital app no longer loses its Loan Screening when this happens, and the tests of the app
run where the services run: see the tracker of the M Capital app, m_capital-izup.

title: [BUG] Exported Print Designer templates fail to render: frappe.parse_json missing in the Jinja sandbox
description: Exported Print Designer templates embed their design (header/body/footer/settings) as a JSON blob and parse it at render time with {% set __pd_data = frappe.parse_json("...") %}. Live example: the Print Format "Sales Invoice - TBS Standard".
notes: Fixed by extending the Jinja sandbox namespace with the JSON helper instead of rewriting the exported templates (and the live Print Format records that contain them): print_designer/utils/jinja_namespace.py installs an idempotent wrapper around frappe.utils.safe_exec.get_safe_globals() that adds parse_json to the sandbox frappe namespace; the shim is installed when the app package is imported (print_designer/__init__.py) so it covers the PDF pipeline, the desk print view and the preview in every process. json.loads is side effect free, so the sandbox stays restricted (no write helpers are exposed). Verified live: the Sales Invoice - TBS Standard format now renders - HTTP 200, a valid 1 page PDF with the invoice content, no parse_json error (previously it failed). Regression test: print_designer/tests/test_jinja_namespace_compat.py (5 tests OK); full Print Designer suites 23 OK (2 skipped) and 194 OK (1 skipped).

title: Milestone invoice of a stock item should prorate the quantity
description:
The milestone invoices keep the contract quantity and carry the portion of the
contract in the rate of the line.

For a service item this is right, a service has no stock and a milestone does
not deliver a part of the service. For a stock item the quantity is normally
prorated by the portion, because a milestone of goods delivers a part of the
quantity.

Evidence on the demo site for a 40 @ 7,500 = 300,000 contract with the
milestones 20/60/20: three draft invoices of 40 @ 1,500 = 60,000,
40 @ 4,500 = 180,000 and 40 @ 1,500 = 60,000. The invoices total 300,000, the
order reaches per_billed 100 and the Sales Order line reaches billed_amt
300,000, so no overbilling was booked.
